evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: `import { toCourse } from '../courses/courses.service';` reuses the courses module's entity-to-domain mapper
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: `@InjectRepository(CourseEntity) private readonly courseRepository: Repository<CourseEntity>` means the service owns course persistence directly
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `entity.enrolled = course.enrolled; await courseRepository.save(entity);` maps the course back to its entity by hand, outside the courses module
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `if (!studentEmail.includes('@')) throw new DomainError('invalid', ...)` puts an enrolment invariant in the service, not in the Enrolment domain object

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: `create({ ...enrolment })` in enrol() and `new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)` in withdraw() map Enrolment inline, with no mapper as used for courses
parsedVerdict.reasoning: EnrolmentsService handles one concern: enrolling and withdrawing students. However, it handles courses inconsistently. To read a course it reuses `toCourse` from src/courses/courses.service.ts, which converts a CourseEntity row into a Course domain object. To write it back, it bypasses the courses module: it injects Repository<CourseEntity> itself, copies the field by hand (`entity.enrolled = course.enrolled`) and calls `courseRepository.save(entity)`. So the rule for mapping a course and saving it is split between the courses module and this service instead of living in one place. Separately, `enrol` checks the student email inline (`studentEmail.includes('@')`). This is an enrolment invariant, but it sits in the application service rather than the Enrolment domain object. If Enrolment validates the email too, the rule is duplicated. Mapping between Enrolment and EnrolmentEntity is also done inline: `create({ ...enrolment })` in one method and `new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)` in the other. No mapper is used, unlike the course path. Confidence is moderate because courses.service.ts and domain/enrolment.ts were not provided.

violations.message: Course mapping is split: enrol() reads the course with the courses module's toCourse mapper, then bypasses that module to write it back, copying `entity.enrolled = course.enrolled` by hand and calling courseRepository.save directly. The rule for mapping and saving a course should live in one place.
The student email check (`studentEmail.includes('@')`) sits in the application service instead of the Enrolment domain object, so the rule is out of place and may be duplicated.
